note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1939. Nominations closed on 18 April 1939 and the Strabane Chronicle prints the complete county council list, division by division, with party labels in brackets: 'practically all the old members being re-elected without any opposition'. The only changes are Coagh (Felix Lavery in place of J. E. Johnston), Newtownstewart (Capt. E. W. Ross in place of Dr. W. Lyle) and Plumbridge (J. Conway in place of Thomas Stewart). The report says the Unionists nominated 15 and the Nationalists 11, but the printed list carries 14 U., 12 Nat. and one unlabelled (Cookstown). No poll took place, so the round keeps the statutory day in the queue (Thursday 25 May 1939), which no retrieved page confirms. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). The same pattern is visible across this county's rounds. See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt Filed on 1939-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (provisional); previously filed under 1939-05-25 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
